Correctness and component-transfer comparison v4

This estimates one local learner’s correctness on generated questions. Audio transcription and learning improvement are separate tasks. Training runs in a browser Worker; only the latest report is persisted in IndexedDB. Report JSON exports contain all fitted models, fixed hyperparameters, training/evaluation feature rows, answer IDs and metrics. The UI can show older v1/v2 reports without relabeling them as new experiments.

Protocol

  • Select exactly one anonymous learner ID and optionally one question task. Restored IDs are selectable and never silently pooled.
  • Exclude records lacking question creation/first playback time, answer time, or required question fields. Deduplicate by answer ID.
  • Select a time boundary near an 80/20 count ratio using times and counts only. Entire sessions whose final answer precedes the boundary form training data. Entire sessions starting at/after the boundary form evaluation data. Crossing sessions are excluded as training/evaluation targets.
  • Features reveal past labels only when their answer submission time is strictly before the current question creation time. Concurrent unfinished questions contribute no labels. Response time, replay count, current answer and current correctness are never features.
  • Train once; freeze weights and fixed hyperparameters throughout evaluation. Earlier submitted evaluation answers can update pre-question history features and both aggregate baselines. This is a chronological online prediction simulation, not a frozen-history test.
  • Compare Laplace-smoothed global rate, condition rate shrunk toward that global rate with four pseudo-observations, L2 logistic regression, shallow CART, and logistic-loss gradient-boosted decision stumps. Conditions include task, key, root, quality, instrument, duration, octave, guitar style, reference setting, actual notes and answer choices; progression conditions include the entire ordered target, actual notes/timing, length, response mode, gap and candidate-generation mode.
  • Fixed logistic settings: 600 full-batch gradient steps, learning rate 0.4, L2 penalty 0.05, unpenalized intercept; bounded predeclared features. No test-based hyperparameter selection.
  • Report Brier score, natural-log loss, five-bin calibration for each method, per-task/key/format errors and observed selection-policy counts. Progression breakdowns distinguish 2/3 chords, four-choice/ordered input, and balanced/random candidates. Format groups include training and evaluation counts. Sampling is the observed question distribution; results do not establish effectiveness of adaptive practice or performance on unseen keys.

Initial data guard

100 eligible answers, five sessions, at least 60 training and 20 evaluation answers, with at least five correct and five incorrect training labels. These are usability guards for an initial experiment, not a statistical power guarantee. A single chronological test does not establish superiority. Repeat on newly collected future sessions; record any subsequent model changes under a new version.

Reproduce / verify

Run node --test tests/*.test.cjs. tests/prediction.test.cjs checks causal feature construction (including overlapping sessions), unchanged weights after test labels change, frozen configuration, deterministic fitting, metrics and learner isolation. It uses synthetic data only.

An exported experiment JSON preserves feature rows and labels for reproducing the fixed fit and metrics with dist/prediction-model.js. Keep the history backup separately for reconstructing features. The export includes private learning history; the app does not publish it.

Key expansion (v2)

  • Model correctness-logistic-v2, features pre-question-keys-v2: add major/natural-minor mode, tonic pitch class and scale degree. Condition aggregates remain isolated by key. The experimental UI can filter by key.
  • Existing v1 report objects remain readable and retain their version. Reproducing a v1 fit requires the corresponding v1 source (commit cd0902220063cc0e2051873485d0dee3bbb4c7a6), because its feature vector has a different dimension. Compare versions on the same future observations before claiming improvement.

Progression records (v3)

Single-chord and 2/3-chord progression records are eligible. A progression target is binary whole-sequence correctness, including order. Per-position outcomes are NOT separate targets yet. Validate progression history with the existing record validator; old 0.1/0.35-second and current 0.2-second gaps remain supported.

Features pre-question-progressions-v3 retain the original pre-question features and append progression length, ordered-vs-four-choice input, gap, candidate-generation flags, prior format performance/count, number of unique chords, and the quality/pitch-class/scale-degree at each of three positions (zero-padded). Format history is only updated from answers already submitted before the current question. The actual target is known to the question generator before playback; neither the learner’s current answer nor position-correctness flags are model inputs. There is no audio transcription model.

Added models

These are small transparent browser-side implementations, not wrappers around external ML libraries.

  • CART classifier correctness-cart-v1: squared-error/Gini-equivalent split gain for binary labels, depth at most 3, minimum 8 examples per leaf, and leaf probability shrunk with 4 pseudo-observations at the training-only global rate. Consider all distinct adjacent training-value midpoints; reject nonpositive gains. Deterministic tie order follows feature order.
  • Gradient boosting correctness-logit-boosted-stumps-v1: logistic loss, at most 40 depth-one trees, learning rate 0.1, minimum 8 examples per leaf, L2 leaf penalty 1. Residuals are y−sigmoid(score), Hessians p(1−p). A split maximizes G_left²/(H_left+1)+G_right²/(H_right+1)−G_total²/(H_total+1). Each leaf’s Newton value G/(H+1) is clipped to [−2,2]. Stop if no positive-gain split exists. Training-only initial log odds use Laplace smoothing.
  • Logistic regression is correctness-logistic-v3 because its feature vector has changed. Its optimizer/settings remain fixed as above.

All three models share the exact same time/session split and feature rows. No model is selected automatically, and no hyperparameters are tuned against the evaluation set. Selection after viewing these results requires another future evaluation window; repeated comparisons on the same window are exploratory. Format-specific results may have few examples or no examples in training; displaying them is not evidence of reliable performance. The overall 100-answer guard does not guarantee sufficient data for each format.

Reproduction and limits

Report schema 2 (correctness-comparison-v3) stores models.logistic, models.tree, models.boosted, the shared feature names in model.features, training/evaluation vectors, labels, fixed settings, five-method metrics and calibration bins. JSON-round-tripped model objects reproduce predictions with predict, predictTree, and predictBoosted from the matching source. The legacy model/calibration fields remain for display compatibility. Earlier exported reports retain their own schema/model versions and are never retrained implicitly.

Run node --test tests/*.test.cjs. Added comparison tests use explicitly synthetic progression data and check all four formats, all five prediction methods, learning a later-position signal, future-label isolation for every fitted model, no current response/replay features, deterministic model fitting, corruption rejection, exported-model reproduction, and the exact Worker import/run path. Synthetic checks establish implementation behavior, not effectiveness for the user. Real learner performance is obtained by running the experiment in the browser holding that learner’s history. Nothing is automatically applied to question selection in this milestone.

Component transfer and paired feature comparison (v4)

The target remains whole-question correctness. dist/transfer-analysis.js reconstructs local evidence from existing answers. Chord identity answers (including explicit “do not know” as incorrect) and non-null ordered progression answers contribute. Chord-quality identification has a displayed root and a different task, so it does not contribute code-identification evidence. Whole-progression four-choice answers never contribute per-chord/pair labels, even if the whole answer is correct. Null/unknown whole ordered sequences do not localize an error and are excluded from local evidence. Stored position flags are not used as features: local matches are recomputed from the submitted sequence and target only after submission. Root-only/unrecognized legacy answers are skipped. Each answer ID is observed at most once.

The common scope is user × key × instrument. A chord root/quality pools identity, two-code ordered and three-code ordered observations, with source counts/rates retained separately. An exact directed neighboring pair pools length-two and length-three answers; the pair outcome is both positions correct, not a causal measure of transition comprehension. Motion families pool signed diatonic degree differences within the same scope. Per-question length/input/position/choice count/duration/register/guitar style/reference/review contexts remain separate and are shrunk toward the common rate. Different durations/registers share coarse evidence; those settings also remain model/context inputs.

Posterior-style smoothing is fixed: a scope rate (correct+2)/(count+4) provides the prior for a chord/pair, then (unit_correct+4*scope_rate)/(unit_count+4) gives its rate; source-specific and exact-context rates use four pseudo-observations at the common unit rate. Counts use capped log1p(n)/log(1001). These are descriptive smoothed rates, not estimated mastery or confidence intervals. Current code/transition descriptors and historic source/context rates are appended to the v3 feature vector. Structural scale difference, actual root MIDI difference, and rendered lowest-note difference are separate: scale degree 3→4 need not be an upward sounding move in a wrapped register or guitar voicing.

Evaluation targets are selected with the existing task/key/session filters. Shared-history context includes all eligible tasks for the selected learner/key, so selecting progression evaluation does not erase prior single-code observations. At question creation, only context answers with strictly earlier submission timestamps can update shared features. V3-style base aggregates still use the same filtered target history as before. All shared maps isolate users/keys/instruments. Future answers, pending answers and simultaneous answers are never revealed early; earlier evaluation answers may update history without refitting any model.

For each of logistic/CART/boosting, fit one version with the original v3 feature vector (baseX) and one with that vector plus shared history and motion descriptors (x). Both use identical target train/test IDs, identical settings and no test tuning. This is an ablation of the entire added history-and-motion block, not proof that shared history alone causes improvement. Report schema 3 (correctness-transfer-comparison-v4) retains both feature vectors, all six fitted model objects and eight probability methods including the two baselines. transferComparison stores per-family Brier/log-loss differences (with minus without); format groups contain both variants. Each model object includes its feature names/version. Saved v1–v3 reports remain readable; they are not silently refitted. Reproducing older feature reconstruction requires the corresponding source version.

The shared-analysis UI works even below the model-fitting data guard. It shows descriptive all-history code/pair/motion and confusion observations with source counts, maximum 12 entries per table ordered by the smoothed rate. The exported sharedAnalysis includes all units and exact contexts (not just displayed entries), plus counts of excluded four-choice/unknown answers. This descriptive snapshot can contain outcomes after the evaluation cutoff; it is never fed into earlier prediction rows. Sparse observations, unequal practice exposure, correlated positions, deliberate repetition and missing explicit ordered answers limit the interpretation. Do not infer that an ascending transition is easier without comparing future matched observations and controlling for the component codes.

Tests cover both directions of 2↔3-code transfer, single→progression evidence, task-filter context retention, scope and duplicate isolation, four-choice/unknown exclusions, strict reveal times, position contexts, scale-versus-sounding movement, paired ablation, frozen models and export reproduction. Adaptive question selection is intentionally outside this change.

Manual tonic permission and evaluation coverage (v5)

ReferencePolicy is the common classifier/validator. New questions carry referencePolicyVersion: manual-reference-v1 and referenceAllowed: boolean; automatic pre-question reference playback remains false. Default permission is on, the preference is persisted locally, and it is snapshotted at session start. The control is disabled during practice and hidden for quality identification. An off question does not show the tonic control and the playback handler rejects calls when off. Review creates a fresh attempt using the currently chosen permission and does not silently replay a historical automatic reference. Source target notes/timing remain unchanged.

referencePlaybackCount is the number of successful reference playback requests before answering. referenceAfterAnswerPlaybackCount is separate; successful post-answer requests update only that field in the saved attempt, preserving ID/answer/answer time and pre-answer count. Cancelled/stale/failed requests are not counted. A playback count does not establish that the learner listened attentively or heard the complete sound. Backup validation checks integer/nonnegative counts, known policy version, and zero reference counts for off/not-applicable questions. Older optional counters are retained, but an absent permission is never inferred from a zero counter or automatic-reference flag. Legacy code/progression questions are unknown; quality identification is na.

History summaries distinguish off, on-unused, on-used and unknown, and each new answer displays before/after counts. Curriculum unlocks remain common (9/10); passed runs retain permission provenance so an on achievement is not represented as an off achievement. Preferences and optional session permission are included in the local workflow; explicit permissions/counters survive history export/import. Duplicate import does not replace existing attempts. The usual optional reference auto flag in old records is preserved as historical data, not reinterpreted as manual permission.

Prediction report schema 4 correctness-reference-comparison-v5 appends pre-question permission on/off/unknown indicators to both base and shared variants. Model/feature versions are bumped accordingly. Exact-condition baselines, mixed-review matching and component-history scope distinguish manual permission. Actual current before/after counts are NOT model features or condition keys. They are used only for descriptive usage-group evaluation. Changing those counters cannot alter fitted weights/predictions. Shared analysis isolates off/on/unknown history; partial pooling across these conditions is not introduced.

The UI filters evaluation targets by permission and retains chronological whole-session splitting. coverageGroups includes the union of train and test formats/permissions, with train count/correct/incorrect, test count/correct and an unseenInTraining flag. Thus train-only single chords and test-only progressions are both visible. referenceUsageGroups reports evaluation metrics for actual use groups; selection into those groups depends on learner behavior, so their differences do not estimate the causal effect of reference listening. Older saved reports remain readable and simply lack the new coverage section until a fresh comparison is run.

Validation includes permission/counter schemas, successful pre/post counting, legacy unknown behavior, mixed-context separation, current-use leakage checks, unchanged common unlocks, explicit on/off component isolation, unseen future formats, and all existing model tests. Browser QA verifies manual on playback, separate before/after counters, off hiding, persisted preference and counters after reload, backup validation, permission filtering and coverage display using synthetic history.

③＋④: related pooling comparison (v6)

Same absolute chord (root pitch class + quality) shares across keys. Original key remains in contexts; scale movement remains key-scoped. Direct evidence stays instrument/user/reference-permission isolated. Chord quality is never merged; old reference unknown remains unknown.

related-pooling.js reconstructs local outcomes from single identity answers and explicit ordered sequences only; four-choice sequence answers and unknown ordered answers never become local labels. Canonical source strata retain key, instrument, permission and single/two/three counts. All relationship weights are recorded separately. For combined borrowing, each source contributes once at the maximum relationship weight:

  • Exact chord across acoustic/electric guitar only.
  • Same degree, key mode and quality across keys.
  • Same root, different quality.
  • Deduplicated pitch-class Jaccard overlap (Am/C = 2/4).
  • Directed adjacent pairs: endpoint similarities, matching actual root direction, additional pair discount. Whole sequence similarity is not used.

Borrowed effective count is capped (initially 4), and direct evidence has prior pseudo-count 4 at probability .5. Borrowed influence is k / (directN + 4 + k). All related rate/count features are attenuated by this influence, so high direct counts diminish related features too. Combined rate is (directCorrect + 2 + k * relatedRate)/(directN + 4 + k). These weights are provisional design choices.

Direct and shared models use the same feature schema and fixed model hyperparameters. Direct vectors use the zero-borrowing profile; direct chord/pair features remain identical in both. Fixed profile: cap4/instrument.6/role.12/root.10/overlap.08/pair.5. Weak: cap2/.35/.06/.05/.04/.5. Strong: cap6/.8/.18/.15/.12/.5.

For each model family independently, outer training sessions are split again using the existing chronological 80/20 session rule. Outer test labels never select profiles. Inner comparison requires the original preparation guards, validation positive/negative counts >=5 and related evidence in at least20 inner training /10 validation targets. Otherwise display deferred/history-insufficient and use balanced profile. Select minimum inner Brier, stable profile-order tie break, refit selected profile on all outer training. Future submitted answers may update causal features; weights and profile stay frozen. Model choice itself is not automated from the outer scores.

Compare regression, shallow CART and boosted stumps for direct/fixed/auto (9 fitted predictions +2 aggregate baselines). Each of instrument/role/root/overlap is also refitted alone for each family to assess added value. These are exploratory comparisons, not causal effects or an additive decomposition. Related adjacent pairs use the enabled relationship in each ablation. Reports retain inner IDs/cutoff/candidate scores, chosen profiles, models, fixed and auto vectors, per-target predictions, family-specific comparison models/predictions, and bounded evidence examples. Fixed, direct and auto metrics always use the exact same outer evaluation IDs.

No adaptive question selection is changed. There is no universal sample-count threshold for trees or boosting; compare future prediction error as history grows. QA covers both selection/fallback, future-label invariance, causal timing, scope isolation and exported auto prediction reproduction.
